A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and visual inspection supports matching equations and figures across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo experiments on MLP kernel statistics, depth stability and activation-dependent finite-width corrections in Section 6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical studies and adds numerical solutions of the finite-width recursions compared with sampled networks in Section 6.1 and Appendix K.1.

M1.justification: The diagram-construction procedure and MLP model remain. However, v3 corrects the computational specification by explicitly centering the cubic-vertex quantity ΔΩ and adding a factor of 1/8 to the V contribution in the NTK-mean correction (v1 Equation 72; v3 Equation 75).

E1.justification: Both versions study initialization statistics using synthetic Gaussian inputs, single and distinct inputs, and MLPs with ReLU, LeakyReLU, identity and GeLU activations. The added convergence experiments retain this coverage; different input realizations, dimensions and widths are setting changes.

E2.justification: The infinite-width kernels computed with neural-tangents and the existing theoretical stability predictions remain the reference methods. The added finite-width curves evaluate the proposed framework; no new competing method is introduced.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix K.1 add a substantial recursion-validation protocol: four-layer GeLU networks, four specified four-dimensional inputs, widths up to 220, double-precision sampling, numerical integration and width-rescaled kernel deviations. These are new experiments alongside the retained stability and activation studies.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic checks of whether the first-order terms explain finite-width deviations. Appendix K.1 isolates the corrections by multiplying deviations by width and tests convergence of V, A, B, D and F against solved recursions. v1 primarily tested depth stability and the presence or absence of corrections.

E5.justification: The new tensor-convergence studies specify 100 repeated Monte Carlo estimates for their means and error bars (v3 Figures 6–10). Existing experiments retain their repetition counts and uncertainty conventions; the addition does not establish increased repetitions for the earlier studies.

E6.justification: v3 adds corrected-kernel agreement with sampled networks at widths above approximately 20, isolated-correction results and tensor-convergence results (Figures 1 and 4–10). Existing stability fits also change: B0101 changes from 0.01ℓ^3.78 to 0.21ℓ^3.34 under the same stated settings (v1 Figure 8; v3 Figure 16).

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 and Appendix E.4 add an all-orders completeness argument beyond v1's selected higher-order checks. Appendix I adds an explicit all-orders argument for the diagonal NTK mean. Mathematical corrections include centering ΔΩ and the factor of 1/8 in the mean recursion. Many earlier derivations are retained under new theorem labels.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the higher-order contribution from selected checks finding no contradictions to a claimed proof of completeness at all orders. The abstract and contribution list also add a general multi-input numerical implementation and its demonstrated predictive accuracy, substantially extending the stated contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix K.1 newly explains why full-kernel plots can conceal inaccuracies in first-order corrections and why width-rescaling amplifies sampling noise at larger widths. The existing interpretations of criticality, scale invariance and the restriction to MLPs are largely retained.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's inputs, estimators and GPU timings, v3 documents the existing NTK parameterization, a SymPy-to-NumPy/SciPy recursion implementation, integration simplification and caching, JAX sampling procedures, integration tolerances, numerical precision and CPU timings (Appendices B, J and K). This substantially expands reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for SymPy, NumPy and SciPy and claims novelty for implementing the general multi-input recursions. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier NTK and Feynman-diagram research otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 4–5 are reorganized around numbered theorems, with substantial application derivations moved into Appendices H–I. Appendix material is regrouped into proofs, implementation details and experiments, and the experimental narrative now begins with solving the recursions. This exceeds local language editing.

P2.justification: v3 adds an introductory corrected-kernel comparison, extensive multi-panel convergence figures and additional theoretical diagrams. It also splits v1 Figure 2 into v3 Figures 3 and 22, moving the NNGP panel to the appendix, and substantially rearranges diagram and figure placement.

improvement.justification: v1 tested qualitative stability and vanishing-correction predictions without numerically validating the solved finite-width recursions. v3 addresses that important gap through direct Monte Carlo comparisons, isolated-correction checks and tensor-convergence studies, supported by detailed implementation instructions and corrected formulas. These substantially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. Section 7 still uses tentative higher-order wording despite the new all-orders theorem, but this inconsistency does not outweigh the concrete gains.
